[32113 Advanced Database | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

Software systems require trustworthy data management systems. This subject covers advanced database concepts, requirements, architecture, design and systems. Current trends and challenges in the practice of data management are explored to develop the robust data solutions. In small teams, students apply these contemporary data management practices to their advanced database project work. Students learn to integrate and manage data from different sources to support the data-intensive software systems.

[32113 Advanced Database | Learning and teaching activities]
The subject is comprised of lectures and workshops. Students will learn advanced data management through hands-on workshops supported by online lecture and reading material. Students are expected to prepare for the lecture and workshop by studying required material in order to participate in-class activities. 

This is a project-based subject in which teams of students will develop a database system to meet customer requirements. So far as possible the customer requirements will be commercially realistic, and the project will be performed in a commercially realistic manner. Periodically students will present their work for review before presenting the finished product for evaluation.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[32113 Advanced Database | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Evaluate data design and management and its value in relation to supporting corporate stakeholder data resource. (B.1)
SLO2: Design data models to support complex corporate stakeholder requirements. (C.1)
SLO3: Create database systems and solutions to support a range of data types and structures to support complex queries and results. (D.1)
SLO4: Collaborate effectively in a group to address a practical business problem. (E.1)
